headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure via MinerU’s MCP/file inputs; no direct evidence of shared workspace or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server, so attacker-controlled document content could reach nuwa-skill through a shared channel if the pair is wired together. nuwa-skill has no documented parser hardening or isolation, so the interaction is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into nuwa-skill as instructions or tool arguments
IF both agents are connected through the same MCP or file workspace
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the agents
Route MinerU output through a plain-text sanitizer
Add a provenance tag to all MinerU outputs
Require manual review before nuwa-skill consumes extracted text
requires-engineering: isolate the agents in separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches document files and can expose extracted content through APIs/MCP, while nuwa-skill has no documented file or data surfaces. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or that nuwa-skill uploads sensitive context, so leakage is possible only if the operator explicitly connects them. The blast radius appears limited to the processed documents.
conditions: IF the same sensitive documents are passed from MinerU into nuwa-skill
IF an operator configures a shared workspace or API handoff
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared handoff path
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Redact secrets before passing MinerU output onward
Log and review all cross-agent transfers
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells, and nuwa-skill has no documented write or git capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource access shown, there is no plausible write-conflict pathway in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is later granted filesystem or git write access
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Do not grant shared git credentials
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory
requires-engineering: add lock coordination if write access is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing extractor, so its outputs can be treated as facts by downstream systems. nuwa-skill is a scientific-research agent with no documented verification gate, making it plausible that extracted text is consumed as authoritative input. That creates a default cascade risk even without direct evidence of harmful actions.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes MinerU output without independent verification
IF extracted claims are used to generate reports or decisions
mitigations: Require citation checks before downstream use
Compare MinerU output against source documents
Insert a human review step for factual claims
Mark extracted text as untrusted provenance
requires-engineering: add automated consistency validation

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. MinerU is open-source and offline-oriented, while nuwa-skill has no compliance claims or sensitive data classes listed, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data under a specific policy regime
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment
Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed
Review vendor compliance statements
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
